name_es: Generación de polígono de límite del sitio
algorithm_pseudocode: INPUT: boundary_polygon_wkt (PRJ_070), usable_area_m2 (PRJ_071)
COORD_SPACE: PLANT (UTM coordinates in m)
ORIGIN: site_centroid (PRJ_052, PRJ_053)
1. Parse WKT POLYGON from PRJ_070 to extract vertices list [(x_i, y_i), etc.]
2. Verify polygon is closed: vertices[0] == vertices[-1] (add closing vertex if missing)
3. Verify no self-intersection: check all edge pairs for intersection
4. Compute polygon area via shoelace (C-COM-002)
5. Compare computed area vs usable_area_m2 (PRJ_071); difference must be < 1%
6. Generate DXF entities: LWPOLYLINE with vertices, closed=True
7. Generate SVG path: M x0 y0 L x1 y1 etc. Z
8. Output entities: [LWPOLYLINE, TEXT (label)]
TOLERANCES: position_tolerance = 10 mm (UTM precision)
COLLISION: polygon must not self-intersect
FAILURE: if self-intersection detected, raise error
failure_conditions: computed area differs from declared by > 1%

name_es: Disposición de implantación del sitio (plot plan)
algorithm_pseudocode: INPUT: boundary (PRJ_070), usable_area (PRJ_071), exclusions (PRJ_073), setback (PRJ_074)
COORD_SPACE: PLANT (UTM m, x=easting, y=northing)
ORIGIN: site_centroid (PRJ_052, PRJ_053) as local origin
1. Compute boundary polygon (GR-COM-001)
2. Compute exclusion zones as MULTIPOLYGON (PRJ_073)
3. Compute setback buffer: boundary.parallel_offset(-setback_distance)  # inward buffer
4. Build Voronoi diagram of equipment positions (if defined)
5. Place equipment pads in available areas (not in exclusions or setback)
6. Generate DXF entities: LWPOLYLINE (boundary), HATCH (exclusions), CIRCLE (equipment pads)
7. Generate SVG with same entities
8. Output entities: [LWPOLYLINE, HATCH, CIRCLE, TEXT]
TOLERANCES: position_tolerance = 50 mm (industrial precision)
CLEARANCES: setback >= PRJ_074 value, exclusion zones respected
COLLISION: equipment pads must not overlap each other or exclusions
failure_conditions: no room for equipment after exclusions

algorithm_pseudocode: INPUT: friction_angle (PRJ_092), bearing_capacity (PRJ_092), cohesion (PRJ_094), groundwater (PRJ_096)
COORD_SPACE: PLANT (m)
1. Compute allowable bearing capacity q_a per C-COM-005
2. For each footing i with load P_i:
area_i = P_i / q_a  # m2
B_i = sqrt(area_i)  # assume square footing
3. Verify footing depth D > frost depth (typical 0.6 m for Peru)
4. Verify groundwater below footing base: D < groundwater_depth
5. For each footing generate DXF:
- RECTANGLE (x_i - B/2, y_i - B/2) to (x_i + B/2, y_i + B/2)
- HATCH (CONCRETE pattern)
- TEXT with footing ID and dimensions
6. Generate section view as ARC + LINE for excavation profile
7. Output entities: [RECTANGLE, HATCH, TEXT, LINE]
TOLERANCES: position_mm = 25, dimension_mm = 5
CLEARANCES: min_distance_between_footings = 2.5 * B (avoid stress overlap)
COLLISION: footing stress bulbs must not overlap significantly
INPUT: grid_voltage (PRJ_111), capacity (PRJ_120), transformer_count (PRJ_125), short_circuit (PRJ_113)
COORD_SPACE: SCHEMATIC (paper space, mm)
ORIGIN: top-left of drawing (0, 0) with y increasing downward
1. Determine number of voltage levels (LV, MV, HV)
2. Place PCC point at top of diagram
3. Place utility source symbol above PCC
4. Place main breaker (SYM-ELEC-001) below PCC
5. Place transformer symbol (SYM-ELEC-004) per PRJ_125
6. Place inverter symbols (SYM-ELEC-011) if applicable
7. Place surge arresters (SYM-ELEC-006) at HV and MV
8. Place grounding symbol (SYM-ELEC-007) at each transformer neutral
9. Connect with vertical lines (line to line, line to neutral)
10. Add labels: voltage level, capacity, breaker ID
11. Generate DXF: LINE, CIRCLE (transformer), POLYLINE (breaker), TEXT
12. Output entities: [LINE, CIRCLE, POLYLINE, TEXT]
TOLERANCES: symbol_position_mm = 5
CLEARANCES: min_text_to_line_mm = 1.5
FAILURE: missing voltage level or transformer count
INPUT: fire_protection_basis (PRJ_130), hazardous_areas (PRJ_131), fire_water_demand (PRJ_136)
COORD_SPACE: PLANT (UTM m)
1. Compute fire water demand Q (C-COM-010)
2. Determine fire water tank location: near property line for truck access
3. Lay out fire water main: loop around perimeter of plant
4. Place hydrants at corners and midpoints of loop, spacing per NFPA 13 (typical 60 m)
5. Place sprinklers in process areas per hazard class
6. Place fire pumps (1 electric + 1 diesel) per NFPA 20
7. Place detection sensors per area classification
8. Generate DXF: LINE (main), CIRCLE (hydrants), INSERT (sprinkler symbols), HATCH (hazard zones)
9. Output entities: [LINE, CIRCLE, INSERT, HATCH, TEXT]
TOLERANCES: position_mm = 50
CLEARANCES: hydrant spacing <= 60 m, hydrant to hazard <= 45 m
COLLISION: hydrants must not overlap equipment

name_es: Disposición de arquitectura SCADA y comunicaciones
algorithm_pseudocode: INPUT: scada_architecture (PRJ_150), comm_protocol (PRJ_151), rtu_count (PRJ_152), control_room (PRJ_153)
COORD_SPACE: PLANT (UTM m) + LOGICAL (network topology)
1. Determine architecture: centralized, distributed, hierarchical, or cloud-hybrid
2. Place control room building at safe location (off-site if remote_both)
3. Place RTUs in each process area per IEC 61400-25 / IEC 60870-5-104
4. Lay out communication backbone: ring topology for redundancy
5. Place fiber optic cables in trenches (share with electrical trenches if possible)
6. Place cybersecurity zones per IEC 62443:
- Zone 4: corporate network
- Zone 3: SCADA DMZ
- Zone 2: control network
- Zone 1: field devices
7. Place firewalls between zones
8. Generate DXF: LINE (cables), RECTANGLE (RTUs, cabinets), POLYLINE (network topology)
9. Output entities: [LINE, RECTANGLE, POLYLINE, TEXT, INSERT]
TOLERANCES: position_mm = 100
CLEARANCES: RTU to high voltage > 5 m
COLLISION: no fiber cable crossing high voltage cable
